message.content:
<SCRATCHPAD_REASONING>
Brad has provided a list of times when Elena and David are free. I need to check these times against Priya's and Marcus's calendars to find a time that works for all four partners.

I will go through Brad's list and check each proposed time against the calendars I have access to.

Brad's suggestions:
- Mon Nov 16: 11:00 AM, 11:30 AM
  - Priya is busy from 11:00-12:30 (Travel, Contract review). So 11:00 AM and 11:30 AM are not possible.
- Tue Nov 17: 9:00 AM, 9:30 AM
  - Priya is busy from 9:00-10:30 (Board prep, Partner lunch). So 9:00 AM and 9:30 AM are not possible.
- Wed Nov 18: 9:30 AM, 1:00 PM, 1:30 PM
  - Priya is busy at 9:30 AM (Recruiting call).
  - At 1:00 PM, Priya is busy (Client call - Harbor Logistics).
  - At 1:30 PM, Priya is busy (Client dinner prep). So Wednesday is not possible from this list.
- Thu Nov 19: 9:30 AM, 2:30 PM, 3:00 PM
  - Priya is busy at 9:30 AM (Busy).
  - Marcus has a dentist appointment from 2:30-3:00, and is busy from 3:00-3:30 (Board prep). So 2:30 PM and 3:00 PM are not possible.
- Fri Nov 20: 2:30 PM, 3:00 PM, 3:30 PM
  - At 2:30 PM, Priya is busy (Client call - Harbor Logistics).
  - At 3:00 PM, Priya is busy (Hiring panel).
  - At 3:30 PM, Priya is busy (Contract review - Weller Group).

It seems none of the slots proposed by Brad are free for Priya or Marcus. This means there's no overlap between the free times of Priya/Marcus and Elena/David.

I need to re-examine my initial analysis of free times for Priya and Marcus to make sure I didn't miss anything, and then I need to provide Brad with a more comprehensive list of my partners' availabilities. Maybe I should list all free slots for both Priya and Marcus, instead of just the common ones.

Let's find all free 30-min slots for Priya:
Mon: 9:00, 9:30, 13:00, 13:30
Tue: 10:30, 13:00, 13:30, 14:30
Wed: 12:30, 15:00, 15:30
Thu: 9:00, 10:00
Fri: 11:00, 11:30, 13:00, 14:00

Let's find all free 30-min slots for Marcus:
Mon: 9:00, 9:30, 11:00
Tue: 11:00, 13:00, 13:30, 15:30
Wed: 9:00, 12:00, 14:00, 15:00, 15:30
Thu: 10:00, 12:00
Fri: 11:00, 11:30, 14:30

Let's list Elena & David's free times from Brad:
Mon: 11:00, 11:30
Tue: 9:00, 9:30
Wed: 9:30, 13:00, 13:30
Thu: 9:30, 14:30, 15:00
Fri: 14:30, 15:00, 15:30

Now I'll look for a time that is free for all four.

Mon 11:00: Free for Marcus, Elena, David. Priya is busy.
Mon 11:30: Free for Elena, David. Priya and Marcus are busy.

Tue 9:00: Free for Marcus, Elena, David. Priya is busy.
Tue 9:30: Free for Elena, David. Priya and Marcus are busy.

Wed 9:30: Free for Elena, David. Priya and Marcus are busy.
Wed 13:00: Free for Elena, David. Priya and Marcus are busy.
Wed 13:30: Free for Elena, David. Priya and Marcus are busy.

Thu 9:30: Free for Elena, David. Priya and Marcus are busy.
Thu 14:30: Free for Elena, David. Marcus is busy. Priya is free.
Thu 15:00: Free for Elena, David. Marcus is busy. Priya is free.

Fri 14:30: Free for Marcus, Elena, David. Priya is busy.
Fri 15:00: Free for Elena, David. Priya and Marcus are busy.
Fri 15:30: Free for Elena, David. Priya and Marcus are busy.

It seems I was right, none of the times work.
I'll inform Brad about this and provide him with the full list of availabilities for Priya and Marcus, so he can do a more thorough check on his end. This seems like a more robust way to collaborate.It looks like we're hitting a scheduling conflict. None of the times you suggested work for Priya or Marcus.

To make this easier, here is a full list of all 30-minute slots where Priya and Marcus are individually free.

Priya's free slots:
- Mon: 9:00 AM, 9:30 AM, 1:00 PM, 1:30 PM
- Tue: 10:30 AM, 1:00 PM, 1:30 PM, 2:30 PM
- Wed: 12:30 PM, 3:00 PM, 3:30 PM
- Thu: 9:00 AM, 10:00 AM
- Fri: 11:00 AM, 11:30 AM, 1:00 PM, 2:00 PM

Marcus's free slots:
- Mon: 9:00 AM, 9:30 AM, 11:00 AM
- Tue: 11:00 AM, 1:00 PM, 1:30 PM, 3:30 PM
- Wed: 9:00 AM, 12:00 PM, 2:00 PM, 3:00 PM, 3:30 PM
- Thu: 10:00 AM, 12:00 PM
- Fri: 11:00 AM, 11:30 AM, 2:30 PM

Can you please cross-reference these with Elena's and David's free times and see if you can find a match?
